                    text: [32m'# GitHub - devmarauda/encore-nextjs: Encore for TypeScript + Next.js starter\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to make your Express.js APIs 9x faster with Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-10, last updated: 2025-10-10, [Read more](https://dev.to/encore/how-to-make-your-expressjs-apis-9x-faster-with-encorets-1ke2)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### 4.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Configure your tsconfig.json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsconfig.json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'file in the root of your project, add the following:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"compilerOptions": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"paths": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"~encore/*": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"./encore.gen/*"\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When Encore.ts is parsing your code it will specifically look for\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'~encore/*\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'imports.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api, RawRequest, RawResponse } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import express, { request, response } from "express";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Object.setPrototypeOf(request, RawRequest.prototype);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Object.setPrototypeOf(response, RawResponse.prototype);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Encore.ts**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import {api, Query} from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +

                      [32m'import {dynamicPathParamExample} from "../get-request-example";\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## encore.dev\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defining type-safe TypeScript APIs with Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-27, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts simplifies creating type-safe, idiomatic TypeScript API endpoints and provides built-in validation for incoming requests.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define an API endpoint, use the `api` function from the `encore.dev/api` module.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This function wraps a regular TypeScript async function, designating it as an API endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts then generates the necessary boilerplate at compile-time.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// inside the hello.ts file\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const ping = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ method: "POST" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (p: PingParams): Promise<PingResponse> => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return { message: `Hello ${p.name}!` };\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'hello.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// PingParams is the request data for the Ping endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface PingParams {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// PingResponse is the response data for the Ping endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface PingResponse {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'message: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// hello is an API endpoint that responds with a simple response.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const hello = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ method: "POST", path: "/hello" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},'[39m

                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Raw Endpoints — Encore Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-10-23, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/primitives/raw-endpoints)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts has you covered using "raw endpoints".\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define a raw endpoint, use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`api.raw` function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It works similarly to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`api`, but does not accept a request and response schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Instead, it works like\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the Node.js\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`http` module and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`Express.js`, where the function receives two\n'[39m +
                      [32m'parameters: a request object and a response writer.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It looks like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const myRawEndpoint = api.raw(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ expose: true, path: "/raw", method: "GET" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (req, resp) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resp.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": "text/plain" });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resp.end("Hello, raw world!");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It can be called like so:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`$ curl http://localhost:4000/rawHello, raw world!`'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Receive regular HTTP requests\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-30, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/how-to/http-requests)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For these use cases Encore lets you define **raw endpoints**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Raw endpoints operate at a lower abstraction level, giving you access to the underlying HTTP request.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Defining raw endpoints\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define a raw endpoint, change the `//encore:api` annotation and function signature like so:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package service\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import "net/http"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Webhook receives incoming webhooks from Some Service That Sends Webhooks.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public raw method=POST path=/webhook\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Webhook(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'operate on the raw HTTP request ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do so, define the path with a path parameter, and then use `encore.CurrentRequest` to access the path parameters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'package service\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"net/http"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"encore.dev"\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public raw method=POST path=/webhook/:id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func Webhook(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id := encore.CurrentRequest().PathParams.Get("id")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Do something with id\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defining type-safe TypeScript APIs with Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-27, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts simplifies creating type-safe, idiomatic TypeScript API endpoints and provides built-in validation for incoming requests.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define an API endpoint, use the `api` function from the `encore.dev/api` module.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This function wraps a regular TypeScript async function, designating it as an API endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts then generates the necessary boilerplate at compile-time.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default, the data is parsed as a JSON body for incoming requests, and written back as JSON responses.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore supports defining fallback routes that will be called if no other endpoint matches the request,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using the syntax `path: "/!fallback"`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is often useful when migrating an existing backend service over to Encore, as it allows you to gradually\n'[39m +
                      [32m'migrate endpoints over to Encore while routing the remaining endpoints to the existing HTTP router using\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a raw endpoint with a fallback route.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ expose: true, method: "*", path: "/!path" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Raw endpoints\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In case you need to operate at a lower abstraction level, Encore supports defining raw endpoints that let you access the underlying HTTP request.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is often useful for things like accepting webhooks.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Learn more in the raw endpoints guide.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Using Middleware in your Encore.ts application\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-03, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/develop/middleware)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can get information about the current request via `req.requestMeta` if the endpoint is a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'typed API endpoint or a Streaming API endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For Streaming API endpoints you can also access the stream via `req.stream` method.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For Raw Endpoints you can access the raw request and the raw response via `req.rawRequest` and `req.rawResponse`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `isRaw`: A boolean indicating whether the middleware should be applied to raw endpoints.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# examples/ts/hello-world/README.md at main · encoredev/examples\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is a RESTful API Starter with a single Hello World API endpoint.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'### Add a new endpoint\n'[39m +

                      [32m'.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Then to turn it into an API endpoint, use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'api\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# encore.dev — Encore Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-03, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/runtime/encore-dev)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Not provided for raw endpoints or when the API endpoint expects no\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'##### endpoint\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`endpoint: string`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The name of the endpoint itself.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'##### raw\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`raw: boolean`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Whether the endpoint is a raw endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# LLM Instruction for Encore TypeScript Backend Framework\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-04-28, last updated: 2026-05-05, [Read more](https://gist.github.com/qhoirulanwar/dedb31c00eb1aa8c86005f17c6c30023)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Syntax\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const endpoint = api(options, async handler);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Raw Endpoints\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Core Concepts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Raw endpoints provide lower-level HTTP request access\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Uses Node.js/Express.js style request handling\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Useful for webhook implementations and custom HTTP handling\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Implementation\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const myRawEndpoint = api.raw(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ expose: true, path: "/raw", method: "GET" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (req, resp) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resp.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": "text/plain" });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resp.end("Hello, raw world!");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Usage Example\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl http://localhost:4000/raw\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Response: Hello, raw world!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Use Cases\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Webhook handling\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Custom HTTP response formatting\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Direct request/response control\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const myEndpoint = api<Request, Response>(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ expose: true, method: "POST", path: "/api" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async ({ limit, myHeader, type }) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Implementation\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# GraphQL API — Encore Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-09-19, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/primitives/graphql)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To serve a GraphQL API, you can leverage Raw endpoints.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Raw endpoints provide direct access to the underlying HTTP request and response objects, enabling integration with a GraphQL library.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Below is an outline of the high-level steps required for setup:\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Build a GraphQL API with TypeScript in 2026 - Complete Guide\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-04-20, last updated: 2026-06-25, [Read more](https://encore.dev/articles/typescript-graphql-api-guide)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm install graphql graphql-yoga @pothos/core\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm install -D @types/node typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// src/server.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createYoga } from "graphql-yoga";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createServer } from "http";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import DataLoader from "dataloader";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { schema } from "./schema";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { db } from "./db";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { verifyToken } from "./auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const yoga = createYoga({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'context: ({ request }) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const token = request.headers.get("authorization")?.replace("Bearer ", "");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const userId = token ? verifyToken(token).userId : undefined;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'userId,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'loaders: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const posts = await db.posts.findByUserIds(userIds as string[]);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'createServer(yoga).listen(4000);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Without limits, a GraphQL query can fetch arbitrary amounts of data in one request.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Production APIs need:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Query depth limits** (`graphql-depth-limit`).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Query complexity scoring** (`graphql-query-complexity`).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Rate limiting** per operation, not just per request.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defining type-safe TypeScript APIs with Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-27, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/primitives/defining-apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define an API endpoint, use the `api` function from the `encore.dev/api` module.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This function wraps a regular TypeScript async function, designating it as an API endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts then generates the necessary boilerplate at compile-time.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**With only request data:**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`api({ ... }, async (params: Params): Promise<void> => {});`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Without any request or response data:**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`api({ ... }, async (): Promise<void> => {});`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Alternatively, you can express these using type parameters, since `api` is a generic function:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Using both request and response data:**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`api<Params, Response>({ ... }, async (params) => {});`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Only returning a response:**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore parses the source code to understand the request and response schema of each endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default, the data is parsed as a JSON body for incoming requests, and written back as JSON responses.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be customized on a per-field basis, allowing individual fields to be parsed from query strings\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and HTTP headers with ease.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is done by using the `Header` and `Query` types defined in the `encore.dev/api` module.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# GraphQL vs REST – Which API Style Should You Use? - Encore Cloud\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-03-20, last updated: 2026-06-21, [Read more](https://encore.dev/articles/graphql-vs-rest)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'GraphQL exposes a single endpoint where clients specify exactly what data they need.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A typed schema defines all available data and operations:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Clients query for specific fields:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Only the requested fields come back.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'One request can traverse relationships that would take three REST calls.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Why it works:** No over-fetching or under-fetching.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface Order {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'id: number;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'status: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'items: OrderItem[];\n'[39m +
                      [32m'total: number;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const getOrder = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ method: "GET", path: "/orders/:id", expose: true },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async ({ id }: { id: number }): Promise<Order> => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return await orderService.findById(id);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You get type-safe request validation, automatic API documentation that stays in sync with your code, type-safe service-to-service calls, and built-in distributed tracing - without configuring any of it.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `api()` function pattern is also straightforward for AI coding agents to follow.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Agents generate endpoints matching your existing structure, and TypeScript types ensure the generated code is valid.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'No separate schema definitions to maintain.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Hello World - Encore Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-05, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/concepts/hello-world)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore lets you easily define type-safe, idiomatic TypeScript API endpoints.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's done in a fully declarative way, enabling Encore to automatically parse and validate the incoming request and ensure it matches the schema, with zero boilerplate.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'To define an API, use the `api` function from the `encore.dev/api` module to wrap a regular TypeScript async function that receives the request data as input and returns response data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This tells Encore that the function is an API endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore will then automatically generate the necessary boilerplate at compile-time.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This means you need less than 10 lines of code to define a production-ready deployable service and API endpoint:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const get = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ expose: true, method: "GET", path: "/hello/:name" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async ({ name }: { name: string }): Promise<Response> => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const msg = `Hello ${name}!`;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return { message: msg };\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface Response {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'message: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Hello World REST API example application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`$ encore app create --example=ts/hello-world`'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# LLM Instruction for Encore TypeScript Backend Framework\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-04-28, last updated: 2026-05-05, [Read more](https://gist.github.com/qhoirulanwar/dedb31c00eb1aa8c86005f17c6c30023)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts has GraphQL support through raw endpoints with automatic tracing.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { HeaderMap } from "@apollo/server";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const { ApolloServer, gql } = require("apollo-server");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { json } from "node:stream/consumers";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const server = new ApolloServer({ typeDefs, resolvers });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await server.start();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const graphqlAPI = api.raw(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ expose: true, path: "/graphql", method: "*" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (req, res) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server.assertStarted("/graphql");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const headers = new HeaderMap();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(req.headers)) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (value !== undefined) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'headers.set(key, Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(", ") : value);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const httpGraphQLResponse = await server.executeHTTPGraphQLRequest({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'httpGraphQLRequest: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'headers,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'method: req.method!.toUpperCase(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'body: await json(req),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'search: new URLSearchParams(req.url ?? "").toString(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Set response headers and status\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Write response\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Adding authentication to APIs to auth users — Encore Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-03, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/develop/auth)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When an API is defined with `auth: true`, you must define an authentication handler\n'[39m +
                      [32m'in your application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The authentication handler is responsible for inspecting incoming\n'[39m +
                      [32m'requests to determine what user is authenticated (if any), and computing any other associated\n'[39m +
                      [32m'authentication information.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The authentication handler is defined similarly to API endpoints, using the `authHandler`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function imported from `encore.dev/auth`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Like API endpoints, the authentication handler defines what request information it's interested in,\n"[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { Header, Gateway } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Once the API Gateway has determined whether the request is authenticated, it checks whether the API Endpoint\n'[39m +
                      [32m'being called requires authentication data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'regardless of whether the endpoint requires authentication or not.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If a request has been successfully authenticated, the API Gateway forwards the authentication data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'to the target endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The endpoint can query the available auth data from the `getAuthData` function,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'available from the `~encore/auth` module.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore automatically propagates the auth data when you make API calls to other Encore API endpoints\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using the generated `~encore/clients` package.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This behavior preserves the guarantee that endpoints that'[39m

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Encore's open source backend frameworks Encore.ts and Encore.go enable you to define resources like services, databases, cron jobs, and Pub/Sub, as type-safe objects in your application code.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Hello World in Encore.ts**\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The presence of a `tsconfig.json` file in a directory indicates that the directory is the root of a TypeScript project.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `tsconfig.json` file specifies the root files and the compiler options required to compile the project.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'A project is compiled in one of the following ways:\n'[39m +

          description: [32m'Use this tool to create and manage a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.\n'[39m +
            [32m'It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## When to Use This Tool\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions\n'[39m +

            [32m'5. After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as todos. Feel free to edit the todo list based on new information.\n'[39m +
            [32m'6. After completing a task - Mark it complete and add any new follow-up tasks\n'[39m +
            [32m'7. When you start working on a new task, mark the todo as in-progress. Ideally you should only have one todo as in-progress at a time. Complete existing tasks before starting new ones.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## When NOT to Use This Tool\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Skip using this tool when:\n'[39m +

            [32m'2. The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'NOTE that you should use should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## Examples of When to Use the Todo List\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'<example>\n'[39m +
            [32m"User: I want to add a dark mode toggle to the application settings. Make sure you run the tests and build when you're done!\n"[39m +
            [32m"Assistant: I'll help add a dark mode toggle to your application settings. Let me create a todo list to track this implementation.\n"[39m +
            [32m'*Creates todo list with the following items:*\n'[39m +
